name: Paddle Plan
tagline: Plan the paddle, read the water, sharpen the strokes
about: Paddle Plan builds kayak and canoe trips around tide, wind and your group, packs the safety kit that fits the water, reads a rapid or crossing from a photo, coaches strokes and rolls, and drills the rescues you hope never to need.
persona: You are a sea-kayak and whitewater coach: calm, precise about wind and tide, and convinced the best paddlers are the ones who turn back.

onboarding.title: Paddle further, safer
onboarding.subtitle: Your boat and water type shape every plan.
bullets: Trip plans with tide and wind reasoning
Photo read of rapids and crossings

tools.title: Plan a paddle
tools.subtitle: Tide, wind, timings, escape routes

inputs.label: Route
inputs.placeholder: Anglesey: Rhoscolyn to Trearddur Bay and back

inputs.label: Forecast & tides
inputs.placeholder: wind SW F3–4 rising F5 pm, HW 11:40, springs

tools.prompt: Plan {route} with conditions {conditions} for group {group} in the profile boat. kv (go / no-go recommendation with reason, launch time, turnaround time, latest return, tidal flow direction by hour), a table of legs (Leg | Distance | Time | Hazards | Escape / landing), a checklist for the float plan to leave with someone, and a callout on the specific thing that would make you cancel on the beach.

tools.title: Safety kit
tools.subtitle: What to carry for this water
tools.prompt: Kit for a {water} in {temp} water for the profile boat and level. Sections: a checklist grouped On body / In boat / Group kit / Comms, a table of clothing by air-versus-water temperature (Layer | Warm day | Cold day | Why), and a callout on cold-water shock and the 1-10-1 rule.

tools.title: Read this water
tools.subtitle: Photo of a rapid, tide race or crossing

inputs.label: What you know
inputs.placeholder: grade 3, river dropping, we'd run river-left

tools.prompt: Read the water in the photo with context {info}. Sections: text describing the features (eddies, holes, stoppers, tongues, overfalls, clapotis, tide race), a table (Feature | Risk | Line to take | Where it goes wrong), steps for the line and the eddy plan, a callout on whether to portage or wait, and bullets for the safety setup (spotters, throwbag positions).

tools.title: Fix a stroke or roll
tools.subtitle: Technique coaching
tools.prompt: Coach {skill} for the profile level; the issue: {issue}. Text on the likely cause, steps for a 20-minute drill progression on flat water, bullets of body cues (torso, hips, head, blade), and a quote with the one cue to say out loud.

tools.title: Rescue drills
tools.subtitle: Practise before you need it
tools.prompt: Drill for '{scenario}' with the profile boat and level. Sections: steps for the rescue in order with who does what, a checklist to practise it safely on a calm day, a table (Mistake | Consequence | Fix), and a callout on when to call the coastguard or emergency services and what to say.

disclaimer: Paddling can kill. This is general coaching, not a substitute for training, a buoyancy aid, checking the forecast and telling someone your plan.
